claims.text: The starting alloy is equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is a chemically random solid solution with minimal inherent short-range order.
The relatively low hardness of simple-solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi is caused by a lack of significant short-range order.
The relatively low strength of simple-solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi is caused by a lack of significant short-range order.
A lack of significant short-range order produces a uniform potential landscape.
A more uniform or less obstructed dislocation landscape facilitates dislocation glide.
Easy dislocation glide accounts for favorable machinability.
Dislocations in the fully random as-cast state encounter few local chemical barriers.
Easy glide in the random state causes low work hardening.
Chemical short-range order increases local barriers to dislocation motion.
Chemical short-range order makes dislocations more wavy and increases local pinning.
Short-range-order-induced dislocation barriers increase critical resolved shear stress or yield strength.
Annealing at 700–800 °C can induce graded levels of short-range order in CoCrFeNiTi while retaining a single-phase solid solution.
Thermally induced short-range order will significantly increase CoCrFeNiTi hardness at both 25 °C and 600 °C.
Thermally induced short-range order will significantly increase CoCrFeNiTi compressive strength at both 25 °C and 600 °C.
Increasing measured short-range order will correlate with increasing hardness and compressive strength.
Strengthening by induced short-range order can preserve a useful balance with ductility.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase equimolar CoCrFeNiTi from 25 °C to 600 °C under elastic-plastic compression, but not after secondary-phase precipitation or excessive ordering.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as an as-cast state, but the control group is described as being produced by rapid quenching to retain that as-cast state. Rapid quenching is an additional processing step and may not reproduce the stated as-cast baseline.

The predicted-outcome field treats failure to create an SRO difference as falsification, whereas the final falsification rule appropriately focuses on samples in which SRO was actually induced. Failure of the treatment to manipulate SRO would not by itself test the proposed SRO-to-strength causal link.
